ch1_fundamentals.topic: Provisions of Partnership Act in Absence of Deed
ch1_fundamentals.question: A, B and C are partners without a Partnership Deed. (a) A contributed ₹1,00,000 capital and claims 10% p.a. interest. (b) B devotes full time and demands ₹3,000/month salary. (c) C advanced a loan of ₹40,000 to the firm and demands 10% p.a. interest. (d) A and B want profits divided in capital ratio (2:2:1). State how disputes are settled.
solution_steps: In the absence of a Partnership Deed, provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 apply:
(a) Interest on Capital: No interest is allowed on partner capital. A claim is invalid.
(b) Salary to Partner: No salary or remuneration is payable. B claim is invalid.
(c) Interest on Partner Loan: Allowed strictly @ 6% p.a. under Section 13(d). C will receive 6% p.a. (₹2,400) instead of 10%.
(d) Division of Profits: Profits must be shared EQUALLY (1:1:1), not in capital ratio.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Section 13 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 governs terms when no deed is executed.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Rent Paid to Partner & Interest on Partner Loan (Charge against Profit)
ch1_fundamentals.question: Lata and Mamata are partners with capitals of ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000 sharing profits in 7:3. Lata allowed the firm to use her property for a monthly rent of ₹2,500. On 1st October, Mamata gave a loan of ₹1,00,000 to the firm. Net profit before rent and interest on loan was ₹1,20,000. Prepare Profit & Loss Account and Profit & Loss Appropriation Account.
solution_steps: 1. Rent to partner (₹2,500 × 12 = ₹30,000) and Interest on loan @ 6% for 6 months (₹1,00,000 × 6% × 6/12 = ₹3,000) are CHARGES against profit debited to P&L A/c.
2. Net Profit transferred to P&L Appropriation = ₹1,20,000 − ₹30,000 − ₹3,000 = ₹87,000.
3. Distribute ₹87,000 in 7:3: Lata = ₹60,900, Mamata = ₹26,100.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Rent to partner and interest on partner loan are charges against profit, NOT appropriations.

    To Rent A/c (payable to Lata)
    To Interest on Mamata's Loan A/c

P&L Appropriation A/c .................................................. Dr.
    To Lata's Capital A/c
    To Mamata's Capital A/c

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Manager Commission Before & After Charging such Commission
ch1_fundamentals.question: X and Y are partners in 3:2 with capitals of ₹1,00,000 and ₹80,000. Interest on capital is allowed @ 10% p.a. Net profit before partner interest was ₹55,000. Manager is entitled to a commission of 10% on the net profit AFTER charging his commission. Prepare P&L Appropriation Account.
solution_steps: 1. Manager commission is a charge: ₹55,000 × (10 / 110) = ₹5,000.
2. Net Profit available for appropriation = ₹55,000 − ₹5,000 = ₹50,000.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: After charging formula = Net Profit × Rate / (100 + Rate) = 55,000 × 10/110 = ₹5,000.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: P&L Appropriation Account with Salary, Commission & Transfer to Reserve
ch1_fundamentals.question: Shiv and Mohan are partners in 3:2. Capital on 1st April: Shiv ₹5,00,000, Mohan ₹3,00,000. Partnership Deed provisions: (a) Interest on Capital @ 8% p.a. (b) Shiv gets salary ₹5,000 per quarter. (c) Mohan gets commission of 5% on net profit after partner salary. (d) 10% of divisible profit transferred to General Reserve. Net profit before adjustments was ₹1,96,000. Prepare P&L Appropriation Account.
solution_steps: 1. Interest on Capital: Shiv = ₹40,000, Mohan = ₹24,000 (Total ₹64,000).
5. Transfer to General Reserve (10%) = ₹10,320. Divisible Profit = ₹92,880 (Shiv: ₹55,728, Mohan: ₹37,152).
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: General Reserve is calculated on the remaining divisible surplus.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Interest on Monthly Drawings (Beginning, Middle, End of each Month)
ch1_fundamentals.question: Calculate Interest on Drawings @ 9% p.a. for year ended 31st March: (a) If Ram withdrew ₹4,000 per month in the beginning of each month. (b) If Shyam withdrew ₹4,000 per month in the middle of each month. (c) If Mohan withdrew ₹4,000 per month at the end of each month.
solution_steps: Total Annual Drawings for each partner = ₹4,000 × 12 = ₹48,000.
(a) Beginning of month: Average Period = (12+1)/2 = 6.5 months. Interest = 48,000 × 9% × 6.5/12 = ₹2,340.
(b) Middle of month: Average Period = 6.0 months. Interest = 48,000 × 9% × 6/12 = ₹2,160.
(c) End of month: Average Period = (11+0)/2 = 5.5 months. Interest = 48,000 × 9% × 5.5/12 = ₹1,980.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Average period formula = (Months left after first drawing + Months left after last drawing) / 2.

ch1_fundamentals.question: A, B and C are partners. Calculate Interest on Drawings @ 10% p.a. for year ended 31st March: (a) A withdrew ₹12,000 in the beginning of each quarter. (b) B withdrew ₹12,000 at the end of each quarter. (c) C withdrew ₹12,000 during the middle of each quarter.
solution_steps: Total Drawings = ₹12,000 × 4 = ₹48,000 each.
(a) Beginning of each quarter: Average period = (12+3)/2 = 7.5 months. Interest = 48,000 × 10% × 7.5/12 = ₹3,000.
(b) End of each quarter: Average period = (9+0)/2 = 4.5 months. Interest = 48,000 × 10% × 4.5/12 = ₹1,800.
(c) Middle of each quarter: Average period = 6.0 months. Interest = 48,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹2,400.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: 4 quarters in a year. Time gap between quarters = 3 months.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Past Adjustment — Omission of Interest on Capital & Salary
ch1_fundamentals.question: A, B and C share in 3:2:1. After closing accounts for the year, it was discovered that Interest on Capital @ 10% p.a. (A ₹10,000, B ₹8,000, C ₹6,000) and Salary to A ₹12,000 were omitted. Pass a single adjustment entry.
solution_steps: 1. Total amount that partners should have received: IOC ₹24,000 + Salary ₹12,000 = ₹36,000.
2. This ₹36,000 was wrongly distributed as general profit in 3:2:1 ratio.

3. Adjustment Table: A should get Cr ₹22,000, wrongly took Dr ₹18,000 (Net Cr ₹4,000). B should get Cr ₹8,000, wrongly took Dr ₹12,000 (Net Dr ₹4,000). C should get Cr ₹6,000, wrongly took Dr ₹6,000 (Nil).
4. Pass entry debiting B and crediting A.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Adjustment Table ensures Capital Accounts balance with zero impact on firm profit.

journal_entries.particulars:

    To A's Current / Capital A/c
(Being adjustment for omitted interest on capital and salary)

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Guarantee of Profit to a Partner by All Partners
ch1_fundamentals.question: A, B and C share profits in 4:2:1. It was agreed that C share of profit will not be less than ₹37,500. Net profit for the year ended 31st March was ₹1,57,500. Prepare P&L Appropriation Account showing distribution.
solution_steps: 1. Standard distribution in 4:2:1 (Total 7 shares): A = ₹90,000, B = ₹45,000, C = ₹22,500.
2. Deficiency in C share = ₹37,500 − ₹22,500 = ₹15,000.
3. Deficiency borne by A and B in their mutual ratio 4:2 (2:1): A bears ₹15,000 × 4/6 = ₹10,000; B bears ₹15,000 × 2/6 = ₹5,000.
4. Final Capital Credit: A = ₹80,000, B = ₹40,000, C = ₹37,500.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Deficiency is deducted from the guaranteeing partners in their mutual sharing ratio.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Guarantee of Profit Borne Personally by One Partner
ch1_fundamentals.question: P, Q and R entered into partnership on 1st April sharing in 3:2:1. P personally guaranteed that R share of profit after interest on capital @ 6% p.a. shall not be less than ₹30,000 p.a. Capital contributions: P ₹4,00,000, Q ₹3,00,000, R ₹2,00,000. Profit before interest was ₹1,74,000. Prepare P&L Appropriation Account.
solution_steps: 1. Interest on Capital: P ₹24,000, Q ₹18,000, R ₹12,000 (Total ₹54,000).
4. R deficiency = ₹30,000 − ₹20,000 = ₹10,000. Entire ₹10,000 is deducted from P personally. Final: P = ₹50,000, Q = ₹40,000, R = ₹30,000.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Since P alone guaranteed R, Q share remains unaffected at ₹40,000.

ch1_fundamentals.topic: Fixed Capital Accounts vs Fluctuating Capital Accounts
ch1_fundamentals.question: Amit and Sumit are partners with capitals ₹2,50,000 and ₹1,50,000. Profit for the year is ₹60,000. Interest on capital is 6% p.a. Drawings: Amit ₹10,000, Sumit ₹6,000. Show Partners Capital Accounts when: (a) Capitals are Fixed, (b) Capitals are Fluctuating.
solution_steps: 1. Divisible profit after IOC (₹15,000 + ₹9,000 = ₹24,000) is ₹36,000 (shared equally: ₹18,000 each).
2. Under Fixed Capital: Capital Account records ONLY Capital (₹2,50,000 and ₹1,50,000). A separate Current Account records IOC, Drawings, and Share of Profit.
3. Under Fluctuating Capital: All items (Capital, IOC, Drawings, Share of Profit) are recorded directly into the single Capital Account.
ch1_fundamentals.working_notes: Fixed method preserves original capital balances unless fresh capital is introduced.
